plants.name: Chrysanthemum × morifolium
plants.description: A long-cultivated perennial with dense, layered pompon, daisy, or spider-form blooms on sturdy stems with deeply lobed, aromatic leaves. It is a short-day plant, so flowering is triggered by lengthening nights, making it a hallmark of autumn gardens in the Northern Hemisphere.
plants.bloomingSeason: Autumn (September to November in the Northern Hemisphere)
plants.location: Cultivated across East Asia, Europe, and North America; native to China
plants.funFact: Chrysanthemums have been cultivated in China for over 2,500 years, and the flower is the national emblem of Japan, where the Imperial throne is called the Chrysanthemum Throne.

plants.name: Jacaranda mimosifolia
plants.description: A graceful semi-deciduous tree with fern-like leaves that erupts into clouds of trumpet-shaped lavender-blue flowers. When the blossoms fall, they carpet streets and lawns in purple.
plants.bloomingSeason: Spring in the Southern Hemisphere (October to November)
plants.location: Native to South America; widely planted in South Africa (Pretoria), Australia (Sydney, Brisbane), and Argentina
plants.funFact: In Pretoria, South Africa, there are tens of thousands of jacaranda trees, earning it the nickname 'Jacaranda City'. In Australia, it is a tradition that flowering jacarandas signal that university exams are near.

plants.name: Colchicum autumnale
plants.description: A bulbous perennial that sends up pale pink-lilac, goblet-shaped flowers in autumn without any leaves present. The strap-like leaves appear the following spring and die back by early summer.
plants.location: Damp meadows and woodlands of Europe, from Britain to the Balkans
plants.funFact: Despite its name, it is not a true crocus. It contains colchicine, a toxic alkaloid, which is used in medicine to treat gout and in plant breeding to induce chromosome doubling.

plants.name: Cosmos bipinnatus
plants.description: An airy annual with feathery foliage and daisy-like flowers on tall, slender stems. In warm regions such as the southern United States and Mexico, it keeps blooming into late autumn until the first frost.
plants.location: Native to Mexico; naturalized and cultivated in North America, Europe, and Asia
plants.funFact: Its name comes from the Greek 'kosmos', meaning ordered or harmonious universe, referring to the symmetrical arrangement of its petals. Cosmos plants are also edible and attract butterflies and pollinators.
